# GEO report: quay-store

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. Both are capped at 40, because `static/robots.txt` blocks Googlebot from the whole site (the GEO-009 blocker).

The raw 48 comes from reading the code. The cap lowers it to 40 because Google's crawler is shut out entirely, whatever else is right. Nothing is unknown, so there is no range. I assumed you want search and AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`. I read all of this from code, not from a running site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Stop blocking Googlebot from the whole site
- **Why it matters:** Google's crawler is told to stay away from every page, including the pages your sitemap and menu point to. This sets off the score cap and costs two rules (GEO-009 and GEO-014, 6 points).
- **Where:** `static/robots.txt:4-5`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: Googlebot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small. Delete those two lines, or change `Disallow: /` to an empty `Disallow:`. The `*` group already allows everything.
- **Score after this:** 18 ÷ 25 × 100 = **72, Good**. The cap is lifted.

### 2. Make page content appear in the server's HTML
- **Why it matters:** Many crawlers don't run JavaScript. With server rendering turned off, they receive an empty page shell for every route (GEO-003, 3 points).
- **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;`
- **Size:** Small. Remove the line, or set it to `true`, so SvelteKit renders on the server (its default).
- **Score after this:** on top of item 1, 21 ÷ 25 × 100 = **84, Good**. Alone, the raw 60 would still be capped at 40.

### 3. Declare the page language and fill the empty description
- **Why it matters:** The `<html>` tag has no `lang`, so the language is unstated on every page. `/shop` has an empty description and `/search` has none (GEO-012, 2 points).
- **Where:** `src/app.html:2` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3`
- **What the code says:** `<html>` and `<meta name="description" content="" />`
- **Size:** Small. Use `<html lang="en">` (or your language) and write a real description for `/shop`.
- **Score after this:** on top of items 1 and 2, 23 ÷ 25 × 100 = **92, Strong**.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `static/robots.txt`: plain, valid lines, tiny file |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access you intend | Problem | Not run | `static/robots.txt:4-5` blocks Googlebot site-wide. Bingbot, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot fall under `*`, which allows all. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/shop` are both blocked for Googlebot by `static/robots.txt:4-5` (0 of 2 routes clear). `/search` has `noindex` but is neither in the sitemap nor linked, so it was left out. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your own domain | Clear | Not run | `/` and `/shop` have absolute canonicals on `https://quay.example`, matching the sitemap and robots.txt domain. `/search` is noindex and left out. |
| GEO-003 | Content is present in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1` `export const ssr = false;` (site-wide). |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and has required properties | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`: the Product block is valid JSON but has only `name`. Google's Product guidance also asks for `offers`, `review` or `aggregateRating`. This is the only route with JSON-LD (0 of 1 clear). |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is referenced | Clear | Not run | `static/sitemap.xml` is a valid urlset, and `static/robots.txt:7` has an absolute `Sitemap:` line. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | Not run | `src/app.html:2` has no `lang` (site-wide). `/shop` has an empty description (`+page.svelte:3`), and `/search` has none. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable by plain links | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5` links `/` and `/shop` with `<a href>`. Whether they are in the served HTML falls under GEO-003. |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | No page-wide `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0`. `+layout.svelte:7` uses `data-nosnippet` on one element, which is a deliberate, scoped choice. No hooks or headers config found. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | Read the layout and three pages. There are no images, links have text, and all three pages have titles. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app is declared. |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (informational, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` found. This is optional and not a problem. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (informational, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. |

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. If you have access logs, `geopilot logs <access log>` checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Server answers:** the real status codes, redirects and `X-Robots-Tag` headers for `/robots.txt`, `/shop` and the sitemap URLs. A live scan would show these.
- **Rendered content:** how much text reaches crawlers (GEO-003 is a Problem from code alone). A live scan would measure it.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`.
- `https://quay.example` is your intended domain. It looks like a placeholder, so replace it everywhere (canonicals, sitemap, robots.txt) before launch.
- `/search` is intentionally `noindex` and is not counted as a problem.
- Blocking training crawlers such as GPTBot or ClaudeBot is a separate choice. This site doesn't block them.
- I read the pages directly and sampled all three routes (`/`, `/shop`, `/search`).

## Outside GEO

Nothing noticed.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
